disclaimer: These courses document Sulandra internal orientation only. They do not replace company policy review, supervisor instruction, hands-on competency validation, professional licensure, certified training, payer enrollment, provider approval, or any training required by a regulator or contract.

courses.title: Sulandra Health Employee Orientation
courses.description: Introduces Sulandra's employment, safety, reporting, and pre-launch operating boundaries.
objectives: Know where to find company policies and support
Separate employment readiness from provider authorization
Escalate safety and compliance concerns promptly

modules.title: Employment and operating boundaries
modules.body: Your employee account, onboarding, and training may begin while a company is still completing licensing, payer, contracting, or other approvals. Being hired does not by itself authorize you to deliver a regulated service, accept a referral, document a client encounter, transport a passenger, or submit billing. Begin provider work only after written authorization, role-specific training, and any required competency or credential checks.
keyPoints: Use the company workspace shown in the portal
Follow your written job description and supervisor direction
Do not treat a training certificate as a license or provider approval

modules.title: Safe work and reporting
modules.body: Review the policies, emergency procedures, reporting contacts, and job-specific expectations supplied by your employing company. Report hazards, suspected abuse or neglect, privacy incidents, harassment, record errors, and scope-of-practice concerns immediately through the designated channel. In an immediate emergency, protect life first and call emergency services when appropriate.
keyPoints: Ask before acting when authority is unclear
Never retaliate against a good-faith report
Keep records in approved systems only

questions.prompt: When may an employee begin regulated provider work for a pre-launch company?
choices: As soon as a portal account exists
After written authorization and required role-specific readiness checks
As soon as this orientation is completed

questions.prompt: Where should company-specific records be created?
choices: On a personal device until operations begin
Only in the correct selected-company workspace and approved system

questions.prompt: What is the first priority during an immediate safety emergency?
choices: Protect life and follow emergency procedures
Wait until the next staff meeting

courses.title: Privacy, HIPAA, and Secure Information Handling
courses.description: Internal privacy and security orientation for protected and confidential information.
objectives: Use only approved communication and storage
Report suspected privacy or security events promptly

modules.title: Privacy and minimum necessary
modules.body: Access confidential information only when your assigned work requires it and limit use or disclosure to the minimum necessary. Verify recipients before sharing. Never look up a person out of curiosity, discuss protected information in public areas, or reuse information across legal companies without an authorized business purpose.

modules.title: Secure handling and incident response
modules.body: Use approved devices, accounts, messaging, and storage. Do not send protected information to personal email, place it in unapproved cloud storage, or share credentials. Lock screens and protect printed records. Report suspected misdirection, phishing, lost devices, unauthorized access, or disclosure immediately; do not investigate or delete evidence on your own.
keyPoints: Preserve evidence and follow privacy-team direction

questions.prompt: What access rule should guide use of protected information?
choices: Access only what is needed for assigned work
Access any record in the organization
Access records when a coworker is curious

questions.prompt: May protected information be sent to a personal email account for convenience?
choices: Yes, if the employee owns the device
No; use only approved secure channels

questions.prompt: What should you do after a suspected privacy incident?
choices: Wait to see whether anyone notices
Report it immediately through the designated process

courses.title: Workplace Safety and Emergency Readiness
courses.description: Introduces hazard reporting, emergency action plans, and role-specific safety limits.
objectives: Use training and protective equipment required for a task

modules.title: Everyday hazard prevention
modules.body: Keep work areas clear, use equipment only as trained, follow lifting and exposure-control procedures, and wear required protective equipment. Stop and ask for help when a task, environment, vehicle, device, or supply appears unsafe. Report injuries, near misses, and hazards promptly so corrective action can occur.
keyPoints: Do not improvise around unsafe equipment

modules.title: Emergency action
modules.body: Learn the emergency action plan for each work location, including alarms, evacuation routes, assembly points, communication methods, and people assigned to assist. Follow instructions from emergency personnel. Plans must be reviewed when you are assigned, when duties change, and when the plan changes.
keyPoints: Call 911 for immediate threats when appropriate

questions.prompt: What should you follow during a workplace emergency?
choices: The location's emergency action plan and official instructions

questions.prompt: What should you do with a newly observed hazard or near miss?
choices: Ignore it unless someone is hurt

questions.prompt: When should protective equipment be used?
choices: Whenever the task, policy, or training requires it

courses.title: Respectful Workplace and Harassment Prevention
courses.description: Explains respectful conduct, accessible reporting, and anti-retaliation expectations.

modules.title: Respect and prohibited conduct
modules.body: Sulandra expects respectful, professional conduct. Harassment can include unwelcome verbal, visual, electronic, or physical conduct related to a protected characteristic, as well as other conduct prohibited by policy. A person may report conduct experienced directly or witnessed. Supervisors must elevate concerns through the designated process rather than attempting an informal private fix.

modules.title: Reporting and non-retaliation
modules.body: Employees may use the reporting options in company policy and should report promptly. Receive concerns respectfully, avoid promises of secrecy, preserve relevant information, and contact the designated reviewer. Retaliation against a person who raises a good-faith concern, participates in a review, or requests help is prohibited and should be reported immediately.

questions.prompt: Which conduct may violate harassment policy?
choices: Unwelcome verbal, visual, electronic, or physical conduct covered by law or policy

questions.prompt: What should a supervisor do after receiving a harassment concern?
choices: Listen, protect against retaliation, and elevate through the designated process
Tell the employee to solve it alone

questions.prompt: How should suspected retaliation be handled?

courses.title: Person-Centered Support Fundamentals
courses.description: Orientation to dignity, choice, communication, and individual-plan boundaries.

modules.title: The person leads the support
modules.body: Person-centered support begins with the individual's goals, preferences, culture, communication, strengths, and rights. Offer meaningful choices, explain options in an understandable way, and respect privacy and dignity. Do not use convenience, assumptions, or staff preference to override the person or the authorized plan.

modules.title: Plan-based support and documentation
modules.body: Provide only supports you are trained and authorized to deliver. Follow the current individual service plan and approved protocols. Document facts, the person's response, and required follow-up without labels or judgment. Report significant changes, risk, suspected abuse or neglect, or plan conflicts immediately.

questions.prompt: What should guide person-centered support?
choices: The person's goals, choices, rights, and authorized plan

questions.prompt: How should support notes be written?
choices: Objectively, with facts and the person's response

questions.prompt: What should an employee do when asked to provide an untrained support?
choices: Pause and obtain authorized direction and training

courses.title: Ohio UI and MUI Recognition and Reporting Orientation
courses.description: Awareness-level orientation to recognize, protect, preserve, and report incidents under current Ohio processes.
objectives: Recognize that routine and serious incidents require different processes
Report immediately without conducting an unauthorized investigation

modules.title: Recognition and immediate protection
modules.body: An unusual incident is an event inconsistent with routine operations, policies, or the person's care or service. A major unusual incident is an alleged, suspected, or actual occurrence defined by Ohio's current rule and guidance. Categories, timelines, and reporting paths can change; use the current DODD rule, company policy, and supervisor or MUI contact. First address urgent medical and safety needs and call emergency services when appropriate.
keyPoints: Do not delay protection while classifying
Alleged and suspected events may be reportable

modules.title: Report and preserve
modules.body: Notify the designated contact immediately and within the strictest applicable timeframe. Record objective facts: who, what, when, where, observed condition, protective action, and notifications. Preserve evidence and confidentiality. Do not lead witnesses, promise a result, confront an alleged perpetrator, or conduct an independent investigation unless formally assigned and trained.

questions.prompt: What comes first after discovering a possible UI or MUI?
choices: Decide the final legal category alone
Protect health and welfare and obtain emergency help when needed

questions.prompt: How should an employee determine reporting requirements?
choices: Use an old memory of the rule
Use current DODD requirements, company policy, and designated contacts

questions.prompt: What should an unassigned employee do about an investigation?
choices: Preserve facts and report without conducting an unauthorized investigation

sources.label: Ohio DODD UI and MUI resources

courses.title: Rights of People with Developmental Disabilities
courses.description: Introduces Ohio rights, dignity, choice, privacy, and reporting responsibilities.
objectives: Report suspected rights restrictions or abuse

modules.title: Rights belong to the person
modules.body: People with developmental disabilities have rights including respect, privacy, communication, relationships, possessions, choices, participation, and freedom from abuse and unnecessary restriction. Services must not make rights dependent on compliance, convenience, diagnosis, or staff preference.

modules.title: Restrictions and reporting
modules.body: Follow the current authorized plan and due process for any restriction; employees may not create informal restrictions. Use the least restrictive, approved response and seek guidance when rights and safety appear to conflict. Report suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation, retaliation, or unauthorized restriction immediately.

questions.prompt: Who holds the rights described in this course?
May an employee create an informal restriction for convenience?
choices: No; restrictions require current authorization and due process

questions.prompt: What should happen after a suspected rights violation?
choices: Protect the person and report through the required process

courses.title: Home Health Infection Prevention Orientation
courses.description: Pre-launch awareness of standard precautions, home-specific risk assessment, and exposure reporting.

modules.title: Standard precautions in the home
modules.body: Treat blood, body fluids, non-intact skin, and mucous membranes according to standard precautions. Perform hand hygiene at required moments and select gloves, gown, mask, and eye protection based on anticipated exposure. Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Follow current clinical policy for sharps, waste, cleaning, respiratory hygiene, and transmission-based precautions.
keyPoints: Hand hygiene before and after care as required

modules.title: Home environment and escalation
modules.body: Before care, assess pets, smoke, clutter, pests, utilities, ventilation, clean-supply storage, and other environmental risks. Keep clean and contaminated items separated. Stop and contact supervision when required supplies or protective equipment are missing or when the environment prevents safe care. Report exposures promptly and follow occupational-health instructions.
keyPoints: Do not proceed without required controls

questions.prompt: Do gloves replace hand hygiene?
How should PPE be selected?
choices: Based on anticipated exposure and current policy

questions.prompt: What should happen when required protective supplies are unavailable?
choices: Pause unsafe care and contact supervision

sources.label: CMS Home Health Conditions of Participation

courses.title: Home Health Patient Rights Orientation
courses.description: Pre-launch orientation to dignity, participation, privacy, complaints, and non-retaliation.

modules.title: Rights in home health
modules.body: Patients must be treated with dignity, respect, and consideration and receive information in an understandable manner. They participate in care planning, may voice concerns, and retain privacy and control in their homes. Follow the current admission materials, plan of care, patient-rights notice, and applicable CMS and state requirements.
keyPoints: Respect the home, property, and privacy

modules.title: Concerns and boundaries
modules.body: Listen respectfully to complaints, address urgent safety needs, and route the concern through the designated process. Do not retaliate, argue, promise a specific outcome, alter documentation, or discourage a complaint. Provide only authorized care within your role and immediately report suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation, or rights violations.

questions.prompt: How should patient information be communicated?
choices: In an understandable manner using required supports

questions.prompt: What is the correct response to a complaint?
choices: Listen, protect safety, and route it through the designated process

questions.prompt: May an employee retaliate after a patient raises a concern?
choices: Yes, if the concern is inconvenient
Only by changing the visit schedule

courses.title: Home Health Emergency Preparedness Orientation
courses.description: Introduces emergency recognition, communication, continuity, and documentation in home settings.
objectives: Follow the patient and agency emergency plan

modules.title: Recognize and respond
modules.body: Know the emergency instructions in the authorized care plan and agency policy. For immediate threats, protect yourself and the patient, call 911 when indicated, provide only assistance you are trained and authorized to provide, and notify the required contacts. Do not exceed your scope or delay emergency care to complete routine tasks.

modules.title: Continuity and follow-up
modules.body: Be familiar with communication failures, severe weather, evacuation, utility loss, medication and equipment dependencies, backup contacts, and missed-visit escalation. After immediate needs are controlled, notify supervision, document objective facts and actions, and complete required incident reporting.

questions.prompt: What takes priority during an immediate home health emergency?
choices: Life safety and appropriate emergency response

questions.prompt: What should guide emergency actions for a patient?
choices: The current care plan, agency policy, and emergency instructions

questions.prompt: When should objective documentation and required reporting occur?
choices: After immediate safety needs are addressed

courses.title: Defensive Driving Orientation
courses.description: Pre-launch orientation to distraction prevention, space management, and stop-work authority.
objectives: Adjust to road and weather conditions
Stop when a vehicle or trip is unsafe

modules.title: Defensive driving habits
modules.body: Drive only when authorized, qualified, rested, and fit for duty. Obey traffic law, wear a seat belt, require passenger restraints, maintain space, scan for hazards, and adjust speed to visibility, traffic, road, and weather conditions. Never text or handle a phone while driving; pull over safely before addressing a device or distraction.

modules.title: Trip decisions and incidents
modules.body: Use approved routes and dispatch procedures. Do not rush to recover schedule delays. Stop in a safe place and contact dispatch when weather, fatigue, passenger condition, vehicle warning, or another risk makes continuation unsafe. After a crash or incident, protect the scene, call emergency services when appropriate, notify dispatch, and follow reporting procedures without admitting fault or altering records.

questions.prompt: What should a driver do before interacting with a phone?
choices: Pull over and stop in a safe place
Ask a passenger to hold the wheel

questions.prompt: What should determine speed and following space?
choices: Law plus current road, traffic, weather, and visibility conditions

questions.prompt: What should a driver do when continuation becomes unsafe?

courses.title: Passenger Safety and Dignity Orientation
courses.description: Pre-launch orientation to secure boarding, restraints, dignity, and trip communication.
objectives: Verify trip and passenger before movement

modules.title: Boarding and secure transport
modules.body: Verify the passenger, destination, trip authorization, and required accommodations. Park and load only in a safe location. Use approved boarding assistance and secure mobility devices and occupants exactly as trained and as equipment instructions require. Confirm doors, lifts, equipment, and restraints before the vehicle moves.
keyPoints: No vehicle movement until everyone is secure

modules.title: Dignity, supervision, and communication
modules.body: Use respectful, person-centered communication and protect trip and health information. Do not leave a passenger unattended unless the authorized trip plan permits it. Contact dispatch when a passenger's condition, behavior, accommodation, destination acceptance, or supervision plan creates uncertainty. Never use an unapproved restraint or convenience-based restriction.

questions.prompt: When may the vehicle move after boarding?
choices: After passengers and equipment are secured as trained

questions.prompt: What should happen when a required accommodation is unclear?
choices: Pause and contact dispatch or supervision

questions.prompt: How should trip and health information be handled?
choices: Protected and shared only through approved need-to-know channels

courses.title: Pre-Trip Vehicle Inspection Orientation
courses.description: Pre-launch orientation to documented pre-trip checks and removing unsafe vehicles from service.
objectives: Complete the approved inspection before service

modules.title: Complete the approved check
modules.body: Before service, use the current company checklist to examine required items such as tires, lights, mirrors, glass, fluids or leaks, brakes and indicators, horn, doors, seat belts, emergency equipment, cleanliness, fuel or charge, lift or ramp, and mobility-device securement equipment. The checklist and vehicle instructions control; this orientation is not the inspection itself.

modules.title: Defects and release to service
modules.body: Document defects accurately. Do not operate or release a vehicle when a defect could affect safe operation, occupant protection, accessibility equipment, or legal compliance. Mark or isolate the vehicle according to policy, notify dispatch or maintenance, and wait for authorized clearance. Never erase or falsify an inspection record.
keyPoints: Only authorized clearance returns a vehicle to service

questions.prompt: What defines the required pre-trip inspection?
choices: The current company checklist, vehicle instructions, and applicable requirements

questions.prompt: What should happen to a vehicle with a safety-critical defect?
choices: Remove it from service and notify the designated contact
Use it for one more trip

questions.prompt: Who may return a defected vehicle to service?
choices: Only an authorized person after required correction or clearance

courses.title: Cybersecurity and Phishing Awareness
courses.description: Protects employee accounts, devices, company records, and protected health information.
objectives: Use strong unique credentials and MFA

modules.title: Accounts and devices
modules.body: Use a unique password or passphrase for Sulandra systems and multi-factor authentication when offered. Never share a password, one-time code, badge, or logged-in device. Lock screens, install approved updates, and use only authorized applications and storage for company information. Contact support through a known channel rather than a link supplied by an unexpected message.

modules.title: Recognize, stop, and report
modules.body: Phishing may create urgency, request credentials or money, change payment instructions, imitate leadership, or use an unexpected attachment or login page. Pause and verify through an independently known contact. Report suspected phishing, credential disclosure, malware, lost devices, or unusual account activity immediately. Do not forward suspicious content broadly or attempt your own forensic investigation.

questions.prompt: How should an unexpected urgent request for credentials be handled?
choices: Pause and verify through an independently known channel

questions.prompt: What is the correct credential practice?
choices: Use unique credentials and MFA and never share codes

questions.prompt: What should happen after a suspected account compromise?
choices: Report immediately and follow security-team instructions

courses.title: Multi-Company Records and Access Boundaries
courses.description: Explains how to work safely across separate Sulandra legal employers and provider entities.
objectives: Confirm the selected company before acting

modules.title: Separate company workspaces
modules.body: Sulandra companies are separate legal employers or operating entities even when they share branding and enterprise tools. Confirm the selected company before reviewing applicants, assigning training, recording employment, handling a client request, or creating an operational record. Access to one company does not automatically authorize work in another.
keyPoints: One employment or grant does not imply every-company authority
The record belongs to the company that performed or employed the work

modules.title: Correct errors and escalate ambiguity
modules.body: Do not solve a company-selection mistake by copying confidential records into another workspace. Stop, preserve the original record, and contact an authorized administrator for correction and audit documentation. When a person has roles in multiple companies, use the company tied to the specific employment, assignment, client enrollment, authorization, or transaction.

questions.prompt: What should you confirm before creating a company record?
choices: The last company a coworker used
The selected legal company and your authority for that work

questions.prompt: How should a record created under the wrong company be handled?
choices: Stop and request an authorized correction that preserves audit history

questions.prompt: Does access to one Sulandra company automatically authorize work for all companies?

courses.title: Care Team Standard Precautions Orientation
courses.description: Awareness-level orientation to hand hygiene, PPE, sharps, cleaning, and exposure response.

modules.title: Standard precautions
modules.body: Perform hand hygiene at required moments and use PPE based on anticipated contact with blood, body fluids, non-intact skin, mucous membranes, contaminated items, or respiratory hazards. Handle sharps and contaminated equipment according to current policy. Clean and disinfect reusable equipment as required before reuse.

modules.title: Exposure response
modules.body: If an exposure occurs, stop safely, wash or flush the affected area as directed, obtain urgent medical assistance when needed, and notify the designated supervisor or occupational-health contact immediately. Follow the exposure-control process and document facts. Do not conceal the exposure or make your own determination that follow-up is unnecessary.

questions.prompt: What determines selection of PPE?
choices: The anticipated exposure and current policy

questions.prompt: When should reusable care equipment be cleaned or disinfected?
choices: As required before reuse and under current procedure

questions.prompt: What should happen after an occupational exposure?
choices: Perform required first aid and report immediately

courses.title: Medication Safety Orientation
courses.description: Awareness-level medication safety boundaries; not medication-administration certification or competency validation.
objectives: Work only within authorization and scope
Use the current order and medication process
Stop and escalate discrepancies or adverse events

modules.title: Authorization and verification
modules.body: Only receive, prepare, administer, assist with, document, dispose of, or otherwise handle medications when your license, certification, delegation, competency validation, company authorization, and the care setting permit it. Follow the current order, medication record, pharmacy label, and approved procedure. This orientation grants no medication authority.

modules.title: Stop points and reporting
modules.body: Pause before acting when the person, medication, dose, route, time, order, label, record, condition, allergy, supply, or instruction is unclear or inconsistent. Protect the person, contact the authorized nurse, prescriber, pharmacist, supervisor, or emergency service as the situation requires, and complete required documentation and incident reporting. Never conceal an error or alter a record to make it appear correct.

questions.prompt: Does this course authorize medication administration?
What should happen when the order, label, and record do not agree?
choices: Pause and contact the authorized clinical resource

questions.prompt: How should a suspected medication error be handled?
choices: Protect the person and report and document through the required process

courses.title: Clinical Delegation Boundaries Orientation
courses.description: Awareness-level orientation to accepting, supervising, and documenting delegated clinical work.
objectives: Recognize that delegation is task-, person-, setting-, and worker-specific
Decline work outside authorization or competency

modules.title: Delegation is specific
modules.body: Delegation does not transfer professional accountability or create general authority. It depends on the current law and rule, care setting, patient or person, task, delegating professional, worker qualifications, training, competency, instructions, supervision, and documentation. A direction from an unauthorized person or an old assignment is not a valid delegation.

modules.title: Accept, perform, and report safely
modules.body: Before accepting a delegated task, confirm the instruction, limits, expected outcome, stop conditions, reporting path, and availability of supervision. Decline and escalate when you are not trained, competent, comfortable, authorized, or able to perform safely. Report condition changes, unexpected outcomes, missed tasks, errors, and questions immediately and document under the approved process.

questions.prompt: What makes a clinical delegation valid?
choices: Current lawful task-specific authorization, training, competency, and oversight

questions.prompt: What should a worker do when not competent or authorized for a delegated task?
choices: Decline, protect the person, and escalate

questions.prompt: What should happen after an unexpected outcome?
choices: Report promptly and follow required documentation and clinical direction
Wait for the next annual review

sources.label: Ohio Board of Nursing RN and LPN FAQs
Ohio Board of Nursing laws and rules
